titleEn: Table Saw Partial Amputation - Tourniquet and TXA

patient.name: Dale Brennan
patient.affectEn: alert but pale and frightened; sitting on the floor gripping a blood-soaked towel over his left forearm; keeps looking down at the hand and asking whether it can be saved
patient.speechEn: full sentences, voice shaky; cooperative and follows instructions; answers questions directly

scene.settingEn: Cabinet-making shop in an industrial park in Surrey, mid-morning. The patient sits on the dry concrete floor leaning against a cabinet beside the table saw. The saw is OFF and locked out. Good lighting, room to work, clear path to the loading door for the cot. One patient.
hazardsEn: table saw - powered off and locked out by coworkers; confirm before approaching
large pool of blood on the floor (about 700 mL) - splash exposure and slip hazard

bystanders.who: coworker (shop foreman) who led you in
bystanders.knowsEn: saw jammed, he reached over the blade to clear it and his glove caught; happened about 8 minutes before you arrived; they shut the saw off and locked it out right away and have been holding a towel on the arm since; he never passed out; foreman called 911; willing to help if told exactly what to do
nothing beyond what the foreman says; can fetch the cot, hold doors, or prepare the amputated-part container under your direction

scene.partnerEn: one partner at your licence level; acts only on your delegation
equipmentEn: sterile gauze and normal saline (for the amputated part)
sealable plastic bag, protective container and ice
PCP: IV start kit and tubing

dispatchEn: 1005 hrs. Code 3 to a cabinet-making shop in an industrial park in Surrey. 52-year-old male caught his left forearm in a table saw. Coworkers report severe bleeding. Hospital is 12 minutes away.
dispatchUpdateEn: Dispatch update en route: coworkers are holding a towel on the arm and the machine has been shut off.
arrivalEn: The foreman meets you at the shop door and leads you in: "He's over here. We shut the saw off and locked it out. We've been holding a towel on it the whole time but it keeps soaking through." The patient is on the floor leaning against a cabinet, a blood-soaked towel clamped to his left forearm. An estimated 700 mL of blood is pooled on the floor around him. Table saw is off and locked out. One patient, good lighting, no other hazards.
firstLookEn: Pale, frightened 52-year-old male, awake and watching you, sitting on the floor gripping a blood-soaked towel over his left forearm. A large pool of blood on the floor. The left hand is attached only by a soft-tissue bridge just proximal to the wrist - a near-complete amputation.

primary.locEn: Alert. Oriented to person, place and time; answers appropriately but is frightened. (AVPU = A.)
primary.airwayEn: Open and clear. Speaking in full sentences, no blood or debris in the mouth, no stridor.
primary.breathingEn: Respirations 22, regular, adequate depth, equal chest rise, not laboured. No accessory muscle use.
primary.circulationEn: RIGHT radial pulse 122, weak, regular. If the candidate reaches for the LEFT wrist: the hand is nearly detached - there is no usable radial pulse on that side (report pulse-on-injured-arm). Together with the pale, cool, clammy skin this is shock.
primary.rbsEn: When the towel is lifted, bright red blood SPURTS from the wound in pulses. If the candidate applies direct pressure through dressings: it does NOT control it - the dressing soaks through immediately and blood keeps spurting around it. Do not suggest a tourniquet. Once a tourniquet is applied proximal to the wound on the forearm and tightened until the bleeding stops: the bleeding stops. If the candidate does not state the time of application, do not remind them (report tourniquet-time-not-noted). The hand is attached only by a soft-tissue bridge just proximal to the wrist. Rest of the RBS: no other injuries - head, neck, chest, abdomen, pelvis, both legs and the right arm are unremarkable; no blood anywhere else. Skin is given automatically during the RBS: pale, cool, clammy. No fall and no head involvement - machine injury only, c-spine not indicated.

history.ccEn: The saw got my hand. It's hanging off and it won't stop bleeding.

opqrst.oEn: All at once, about eight minutes before you got here - around 0957 - the saw jammed, I reached over the blade to clear it, my glove caught and it pulled my arm in.
opqrst.pEn: Nothing makes it better. Moving the arm or pressing on it makes it worse.
opqrst.qEn: Deep, throbbing, burning. Like it's on fire.
opqrst.rEn: It stays in the wrist and forearm. It doesn't go anywhere else.
opqrst.sEn: Nine out of ten. Worst pain I have ever had.
opqrst.tEn: Since it happened - constant, it hasn't let up at all.

sample.sEn: My hand is nearly cut off and I've bled a lot. I feel lightheaded, my heart is pounding, and I'm a bit sick to my stomach.
sample.aEn: Sulfa drugs - they give me hives. Nothing else that I know of.
sample.mEn: Metformin for my sugar and atorvastatin for cholesterol. I take them every morning.
sample.pEn: Type 2 diabetes and high cholesterol. Nothing else - no heart problems, no bleeding problems, no surgeries.
sample.lEn: Breakfast at 0700 - eggs and toast - and coffee since then. Nothing else.
sample.eEn: I was cutting panels and the saw jammed. I reached over the blade to clear it, my glove caught and it pulled my arm in. I didn't pass out and nothing else touched the blade - just the left arm.

fe.generalEn: I felt really lightheaded sitting on the floor back there. No fever, no illness lately, no weight change.
fe.cnsEn: No headache, no dizziness apart from feeling lightheaded, no numbness or weakness anywhere else, I never blacked out.
fe.respiratoryEn: No trouble breathing, no cough, no chest tightness.
fe.cardiovascularEn: My heart is pounding. No chest pain, no palpitations before today.
fe.giGuEn: I feel nauseated. No vomiting, no belly pain, no bowel or bladder problems.
fe.integumentaryEn: Just the wound on my arm. No other cuts, no rashes, no bruising elsewhere.
fe.musculoskeletalEn: Nothing else hurts - no neck or back pain, my legs are fine, the right arm is fine.
fe.endocrineEn: The diabetes is well controlled - I check my sugars and they've been fine. No thyroid problems.
fe.eentEn: No problems with my eyes, ears, nose or throat. Nothing got in my eyes.

findings.headNeckEn: No injuries. No lacerations, no deformity, no tenderness of the scalp, face or neck. Trachea midline, no JVD. Pupils equal and reactive.
findings.chestLungsEn: Chest clear with equal air entry in all 6 sites on auscultation. No tenderness, no deformity, equal rise and fall.
findings.abdomenEn: Soft, non-tender in all four quadrants, no distension, no bruising.
findings.backEn: No tenderness, no deformity, no wounds. (Log-roll not required - no spinal mechanism.)
findings.lowerExtremitiesEn: No injuries. No deformity or tenderness; moves both legs; distal circulation, sensation and movement present in both feet.
findings.upperExtremitiesEn: LEFT: tourniquet in place on the forearm, bleeding controlled, dressing dry with no strike-through. Distal part cool and pulseless - expected distal to a tourniquet. Hand attached only by a soft-tissue bridge just proximal to the wrist. RIGHT arm: normal, no injury, radial pulse present; this is the arm for the BP cuff, SpO2 probe and IV.

vitalsSets.unlockNoteEn: en route; after TXA / after loading / or at 10 minutes - improving with fluids (PCP) or with hemorrhage control, warmth and O2 (EMR)

stateChanges.examinerLineEn: The towel is now soaked through and dripping onto the floor. The patient is visibly more pale and his pulse is faster and harder to feel. He says: "I feel like I'm going to pass out."
As soon as the tourniquet is loosened, bright red blood spurts from under the dressing again and the patient becomes more pale and more frightened.

expected.actionEn: Acknowledge; plan tourniquet, pressure dressings, oxygen, amputated-part care, early transport
triggers: plan for tourniquet and pressure dressings
this will be a load and go

expected.actionEn: Anticipate machine hazard and blood exposure; PPE incl eye protection
triggers: make sure the saw is off

expected.actionEn: Verbalize hazards (machine locked out, blood), environment, MOI (table saw), one patient; estimate blood loss
triggers: how much blood is on the floor

expected.actionEn: Don gloves and eye protection (splash risk)
First look: pale male, awake, large blood pool, near-complete amputation at the wrist
Attempt direct pressure; when it fails, apply a tourniquet proximal to the wound, tighten to stop the bleed, NOTE THE TIME, do not release

triggers: talking so the airway is clear

expected.actionEn: Assess circulation on the uninjured side; recognize shock
triggers: rate and quality of the pulse

expected.actionEn: Complete the RBS for other injuries
triggers: head to toe for other injuries
check the rest of the body

expected.actionEn: Position supine, keep warm with blankets
Bandage the wound once hemorrhage is controlled
Categorize as RTC and act with urgency
Packaged and ready to load within 15 minutes
Delegate bystanders effectively (cot, doors, part preservation under direction)
triggers: get a bag ready for the hand

expected.actionEn: HxC/C: mechanism, time of injury (critical for TXA window), blade contact points, LOC
BP by auscultation on the uninjured arm
BGL - indicated in a known diabetic

triggers: run my hands down the back

expected.actionEn: Upper extremities: tourniquet site, dressing, wound recheck
Wound management skill: tourniquet technique correct, time noted, bleeding controlled, wound bandaged
triggers: two to three inches above the wound
write the time on the tourniquet

expected.actionEn: Preserve the amputated part correctly (moist sterile gauze, bag, kept cool, not on ice, transported with patient)
triggers: wrap the hand in moist gauze
transport the part with the patient

expected.actionEn: Execute the Hypovolemia protocol (supine, warm, O2, rapid transport)
PCP: IV, 20 mL/kg bolus reassessed q500 mL, and TXA 2 g IV over 1 min with 6 rights
triggers: vascular access on the right arm

expected.actionEn: Verbalize withholding Entonox due to shock caution
Reassess ABCs plus tourniquet/dressing after each move and each 500 mL
Second full vitals within 5-6 minutes; interpret the improving trend
Never release or loosen the tourniquet
Complete hand-off incl part preservation and drug times
Accurate PCR within 5 minutes (tourniquet and TXA times documented)

specialEvents.descriptionEn: candidate loosens, releases, converts or removes the tourniquet at any time after it is applied (including 'to check if it is still bleeding')
tourniquet applied but the candidate never states, writes or asks the time of application
tourniquet placed distal to the wound or over the wrist / soft-tissue bridge, not tightened until the bleeding stops, or not secured (e.g. windlass left loose)
candidate has seen the spurting bleed (towel lifted / direct pressure failed) and moves on to airway, breathing, vitals, history, oxygen or packaging while it is still uncontrolled
candidate places the amputated part directly on ice, in water, in dry ice, or warms it
candidate leaves the amputated part at the scene or does not transport it with the patient
candidate administers Entonox to this patient despite the shock caution (log drug:entonox as well)
candidate assesses the pulse, BP or SpO2 on the injured left arm, or tries to start the IV in it
PCP runs the saline bolus past 500 mL or onto the next bag without reassessing the patient (BP / vitals / ABCs) in between
candidate lets the patient stand up or walk to the cot

drugs.doseEn: 2 g (2000 mg) IV push over 1 minute - single dose
drugs.indicationsEn: shock secondary to blood loss after initiating the Hypovolemia protocol; injury at approximately 0957 is well inside the 3-hour window
drugs.contraindicationsEn: known hypersensitivity or allergy to TXA; more than 3 hours after injury; patient under 12 years; isolated TBI
drugs.cautionsEn: further hypotension if administered too quickly

drugs.doseEn: 20 mL/kg IV bolus to a maximum of 2 L, reassessing after every 500 mL; target systolic BP 90
self-administered by inhalation - WITHHELD in this scenario: Entonox is cautioned in shock (if given, report drug:entonox and entonox-given-in-shock)

notificationFacts.cc: near-complete amputation of the left hand just proximal to the wrist with arterial bleeding
notificationFacts.moi: table saw - glove caught and the arm was pulled into the blade at approximately 0957
notificationFacts.hxcc: direct pressure failed; tourniquet applied to the left forearm at 1012 and not released; estimated 700 mL blood loss on scene; no LOC; pain 9/10
notificationFacts.vitals: GCS 15, BP 96/64, pulse 122 weak regular, resps 22, skin pale cool clammy, SpO2 95% on 15 L NRB, BGL 7.8
notificationFacts.treatments: tourniquet at 1012, pressure dressing, supine with warmth, high-flow oxygen; PCP: IV with normal saline bolus running, TXA 2 g IV at 1025; amputated part wrapped in saline-moistened gauze, bagged, kept cool, coming with the patient
notificationFacts.findings: shock from blood loss; no other injuries; ETA about 12 minutes

handoffFacts.cc: near-complete amputation of the left hand just proximal to the wrist, arterial bleeding uncontrolled by direct pressure
handoffFacts.moi: table saw - reached over the blade to clear a jam, glove caught and the arm was pulled in, at approximately 0957
handoffFacts.hxcc: no LOC; nothing else touched the blade; pain 9/10; estimated 700 mL blood loss on scene; tourniquet applied to the left forearm at 1012 and has not been released
handoffFacts.initialVitals: GCS 15, BP 96/64, pulse 122 weak regular, resps 22, skin pale cool clammy, pupils equal and reactive, SpO2 95% on 15 L NRB, BGL 7.8
handoffFacts.finalVitals: GCS 15, BP 102/66, pulse 114 weak regular, resps 20, skin pale cool, SpO2 96% on 15 L NRB - improving (PCP: after one litre of saline)
handoffFacts.treatments: tourniquet at 1012 (never released), pressure dressing over the wound, supine with warmth, high-flow oxygen; PCP: IV on the right arm, normal saline bolus reassessed every 500 mL, TXA 2 g IV at 1025; amputated part rinsed, wrapped in saline-moistened sterile gauze, bagged, kept cool, transported with the patient; Entonox withheld (shock caution)
handoffFacts.findings: estimated 700 mL blood loss; shock improving; distal part cool and pulseless below the tourniquet (expected); dressing dry; no other injuries

pcrFacts.cc: Near-complete left hand amputation proximal to wrist, arterial hemorrhage
pcrFacts.hxcc: Table saw caught glove while clearing jam ~0957; no LOC; pain 9/10; ~700 mL loss on scene
treatments: Direct pressure failed - tourniquet left forearm at 1012, never released
Part: saline-moist gauze, bagged, kept cool, transported with patient
PCP: IV, NS bolus q500 mL reassess, TXA 2 g IV at 1025
findings: Shock: BP 96/64, pulse 122, pale cool clammy
pcrFacts.vitals: Set 1 (baseline, tourniquet on): GCS 15, BP 96/64, P 122 weak regular, R 22, skin pale cool clammy, PERL, SpO2 95% on 15 L NRB, BGL 7.8 mmol/L. Set 2 (en route): GCS 15, BP 102/66, P 114 weak regular, R 20, skin pale cool, PERL, SpO2 96% on 15 L NRB
pcrFacts.times: injury approximately 0957; tourniquet applied 1012 (never released); PCP: TXA 2 g IV 1025

examinerPrompts.missedInjuryEn: You have dealt with the left arm - what did the rest of your rapid body survey show? What about the head, chest, abdomen, pelvis, legs and the right arm?

trackNotes.emrEn: EMR: tourniquet, part preservation, shock positioning, warmth, high-flow O2 and a 15-minute clock are all EMR-level skills - no IV, no TXA. Entonox withheld (shock caution).
trackNotes.pcpEn: PCP adds vascular access on the intact arm, 20 mL/kg NS bolus (max 2 L, reassess q500 mL, target SBP 90) and TXA 2 g IV over 1 minute within the 3-hour window. Functional Enquiry en route.

sourcePages: scenario tr-04 (data/practical/scenarios.json); BC Provincial Examination Guidelines (current to June 15, 2026): p.7 RTC criteria (hemorrhage requiring tourniquet application; amputation proximal to wrist; cool pale clammy skin secondary to suspected shock), p.19 Wound Care / Hemorrhage Control (direct pressure, then tourniquet proximal to the wound if direct pressure fails; note the time and do not release once applied; bandage once controlled), p.20 Preservation of Amputated Parts (rinse with cool sterile water, saline-moistened sterile gauze, plastic bag, keep cool, transport with patient; never warm, never in water, never directly on ice, never dry ice), p.54 Hypovolemia (control hemorrhage, supine, keep warm, oxygen; PCP: vascular access, fluid bolus 20 mL/kg to a maximum of 2 L reassessing every 500 mL, consider TXA in shock secondary to blood loss), p.65 Entonox (caution: shock), p.78 Tranexamic Acid (2 g / 2000 mg IV push over 1 minute; contraindicated if more than 3 hours after injury, under 12 years, isolated TBI)
